notes: Spec asserts: a live parent + in-flight subagent, then a SIGKILL on the shared OS process (muse's subagents run in-process and share the parent's PID), and both sessions eventually disappear without either ever spuriously transitioning to working/waiting during cleanup (issue #321 invariant). Muse's children share the parent's PID, which is the exact trigger shape of open bug #1962 (pidMonitor.watched map[int]string is last-write-wins per PID) — cited in this cell's metadata.json caveats, not re-derived here. #1962 only affects WHICH path (kqueue-fast vs PIDManager.CheckPIDLiveness's independent per-session ESRCH sweep, <=~15s worst case) reaps whichever session the kqueue race starves, not whether it eventually happens, so parent_cleanup and child_cleanup below carry a generous max_delay_ms rather than assuming near-simultaneous kqueue delivery for both. Session-birth shape (single-birth vs a transient proc-<PID> presession) follows 2-13_turn-end-terminal-text's live-confirmed pattern for muse: the real parent session is born directly into ready.

text: Parent session appears in ready shortly after muse's TUI finishes launching (single-birth per 2-13's live-confirmed pattern)
The delegation prompt drives the parent ready → working
The delegated subagent's own transcript materializes under <parent>/subagent/<child-id>/session.jsonl
Detector binds the child's ParentSessionID to the parent's session id (format-spec §9: subagent.control.child_session_bound / adapter-derived ParentSessionIDFromPath)
The subagent starts working immediately — subagents skip a ready birth and start directly at working (2-13's live-confirmed finding)

SIGKILL on the shared OS process (parent and child share one PID): pid_manager emits process_exited for the parent session id — either via the kqueue fast path, or (if #1962 starves it) via PIDManager.CheckPIDLiveness's independent per-session ESRCH sweep

invariants: no state_transition to working for the parent after child_turn_start
no state_transition to waiting for the parent after child_turn_start
no state_transition to working for the child after child_turn_start
no state_transition to waiting for the child after child_turn_start
text: The orphaned child is reaped without a spurious working/waiting transition on either session during cleanup (issue #321 invariant) — again via either the kqueue fast path or the redundant ESRCH sweep, whichever #1962's shared-PID race leaves for it
